_doc: Single declarative taxonomy graph. Each term carries surface forms (incl. Czech variants), categories, role-family votes, and signal tags. All keyword scans across profiling/insights/ats/gemini query this graph. Surface forms are matched after NFC normalization + casefold; both literal and word-compact forms are checked. v3 adds optional `parents`: ids of broader/superset skills (a child is a specialization, e.g. swiftui -> swift, fastapi -> python). The matching engine (taxonomy.py::skill_match_score) uses these edges so a foundational/adjacent skill counts as a partial match instead of a miss. Parent ids must be existing term ids. Sources are listed at the bottom of README.md.

role_families.software_engineering: Software development & engineering — developers, SWEs, DevOps/SRE, QA automation, mobile/web/backend/frontend.
role_families.data_ai: Data, analytics & AI/ML — data engineers/scientists, ML engineers, analysts, BI.
role_families.product_project: Product & project/program management — PMs, product owners, project/program managers, scrum masters, business analysts.
role_families.healthcare_clinical: Healthcare & clinical care — nurses, physicians, allied health, care workers (licensure/credentialing common).
role_families.life_sciences_research: Science & research — scientists, researchers, lab/R&D, pharma/biotech, technical research.
role_families.skilled_trades: Skilled trades & craft — electricians, welders, machinists, mechanics, construction trades, field technicians (certs/licenses common).
role_families.operations_logistics: Operations, logistics & production — warehouse, supply chain, drivers/fleet, dispatch, manufacturing production/assembly, plant ops.
role_families.frontline_service: Frontline & service — retail, hospitality, food service, front desk, hourly customer-facing roles.
role_families.sales_marketing: Sales & marketing — sales reps, account managers, business development, marketing, brand, growth.
role_families.finance_accounting: Finance & accounting — accountants, controllers, auditors, financial/credit analysts, actuaries, underwriters, banking roles.
role_families.legal_compliance: Legal, risk & compliance — lawyers, paralegals, compliance/risk officers, regulatory affairs.
role_families.hr_people: HR & people — recruiters, talent acquisition, HR business partners, people operations, L&D.
role_families.education_academic: Education & academia — teachers, professors, lecturers, instructors, faculty, academic staff.
role_families.creative_design: Creative & design — graphic/UX/UI designers, copywriters, content/editorial, producers, photographers, creative direction.
role_families.customer_support: Customer support & success — support agents, customer service, help desk, customer success.
role_families.general_professional: General professional / other — office, administrative, coordination, consulting, and any white-collar role not covered by a more specific family. The default fallback.

_doc_family_heuristics: family_degree_terms + adjacent_domain_signals are the role-family-keyed surface heuristics behind the early-career/career-switcher transform (pipeline/jobfit/transform.py::compute_potential and transferable.py::domain_distance). family_degree_terms: substrings (CZ+EN, lowercased) that hint a candidate's degree/education_detail is relevant to the target family, lifting the potential 'foundation' term. adjacent_domain_signals: prior-role surface signals (matched against a switcher's job/internship evidence) that sit ADJACENT to the target family, so the domain-distance grade sees a short bridge (finance analyst -> data work) vs a far one. Both cover all role_families so 13 non-tech families are no longer silently degraded to a bare fallback. The software_engineering/data_ai/product_project values preserve the original hardcoded tech lists exactly.
_doc_language_aliases: language_aliases maps a canonical language key to the lowercased needle substrings that satisfy a requirement for it in the KO filter / language-coverage blend (pipeline/jobfit/matching.py::_has_language) — so a candidate listing 'Czech (native)' or 'čeština' still satisfies a 'Czech' requirement. Moved out of a hardcoded matching.py dict so a new required language is config, not code; matching.py's raw-matching fallback only fires for a required language with no bucket here. taxonomy.py loads + validates it (non-empty language -> non-empty list of LOWERCASE string needles — _has_language casefolds the haystack, so an uppercase needle could never match). The original four hardcoded buckets (english/czech/german/slovak) are preserved exactly; the rest are practical EU languages (polish/hungarian/romanian/french/spanish/italian/dutch/ukrainian), each carrying an English name, a Czech stem (covering -ština/-sky declensions) and the native surface form.

enterprise/corporate.rationale: Multinational R&D centres in Prague pay 30–40% above local mid-market on guaranteed comp; bonuses/equity add another 20–30%. Source: Kitalent Prague ICT analysis.

scaleup.rationale: Scaleups (Productboard, Rohlik, Keboola tier) sit between startups and multinationals: above startups for proven delivery, below corporate on cash, with upside tied to growth.

startup.rationale: Early-stage CZ startups compress cash salary and lean on equity/upside. Graduate entry at startups is materially below large-company entry. Source: expats.cz salary surveys.

agency/consultancy.rationale: Mixed signal: Big-4/MBB consultants reach corporate-mid levels (Accenture Prague 83–91k); local consultancies (Deloitte CZ junior 44–58k) sit below in-house corporate IT. Net is roughly market-neutral.

public sector.rationale: Czech public-sector IT capped by státní tarify (state pay tables); 80% of public-admin earn 29.8–65.0k vs 80% of IT earning 45–126k. Public sector also retained the abolished guaranteed-wage system in Jan 2025, widening the gap. Sources: platy.cz, expats.cz.

remote.rationale: International or fully-remote hiring opens access to higher cash bands than local-only postings.

equity.rationale: Equity/options should be evaluated separately from cash compensation; no cash-band adjustment.

regulated.rationale: Czech banking, fintech, pharma and healthtech roles trade at premium vs unregulated tech, reinforced by NIS2 (Nov 2025) and DORA (Jan 2025) compliance workload.

english.rationale: English proficiency is a baseline requirement at multinational R&D centres in Prague; effectively an entry-floor signal at senior level.

leadership.rationale: Leadership/mentoring evidence is the steepest non-skill premium in the data; Prague senior managers reach 167k+ CZK and VP Engineering at multinationals 220–350k+ CZK.

cloud.rationale: Cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP/IaC) is repeatedly cited as the top skills-gap by Czech CIOs; named premia attached to certifications. Source: Kitalent, Nucamp 2025.

ai.rationale: AI/LLM skills carry a 15–25% premium in the local market and are projected at 10–12% annual salary inflation through 2026 vs 6–8% for general ICT.

security.rationale: Czech New Cybersecurity Act (Nov 2025, NIS2 transposition) and DORA (Jan 2025) widened a pre-existing 10k+ specialist shortage; movers report 25–35% premia.

devops.rationale: DevOps Engineer 62k–155k CZK on platy.cz — among the highest IT-role bands. 29% of CZ IT teams hired a DevOps engineer in the last cycle; cloud/IaC is table stakes.

german.rationale: German is the second-most-cited language in CZ shared-service centres after English (Škoda/VW, Siemens, Erste, ČSOB nearshoring); modest cash premium, weighted at roughly half of English.

regulated_industry.rationale: Banking/fintech/pharma roles in CZ pay above general tech average (~74k IT industry vs 100k+ at mid-level in regulated sectors); compliance experience compounds with NIS2/DORA/MiCA workload in 2025–2026.
